I01.why: Both find intercepts of a standard-form line (2x+5y=20, asks a-b); I01 reverses it: given the intercept sum, solve for k.

I02.why: Both ask for the greatest whole number under an 'at most $' budget inequality; I02 adds a second item with a minimum-quantity constraint (two variables), which changes the setup.

I05.why: Same multiplier arithmetic (x1.20 then a decrease, net percent change), but ACT-007 is a price changed twice in a row and I05 is area from two dimensions.
Percent change in area from changes in length; ACT-175 scales one circle radius, I05 changes two rectangle dimensions in opposite directions.

I06.why: Area of a 30-60-90 triangle from one given side; ACT-504 gives the hypotenuse 12, I06 gives the longer leg 9. Same ratio-then-area reasoning.

I07.why: Both compare exponential 2^x with linear functions; ACT-145 counts integers where 2^x >= 4x, I07 evaluates several functions at x=10.

I08.why: Both find an unknown coordinate of a point lying on a line; SAT-118 builds the line from two points with a fixed y, I08 substitutes (a, a+3) into a given equation.

I09.why: Sine of an acute angle in a right triangle from its two legs (8 and 15); I09 puts it on coordinates with legs 8 and 6 and needs the hypotenuse 10.

I10.why: Two consecutive positive even integers with a quadratic condition (sum of squares 340), asks for the larger; I10 uses odd integers and a product of 195, with the same n(n+2) quadratic.

I11.why: Same mixture template: a starting amount at one concentration, add x to reach a target percent, solve for x. I11 is the pure-addition (100%) case with shirts in place of acid.

I12.why: Rectangular prism volume = l*w*h; SAT-085 runs it backward (height from volume).

I13.why: Value of k that makes a linear equation have no solution; ACT-161 has k on the x-coefficient, I13 has k in the constant (the coefficients already match).
Same no-solution condition (equal slopes, different constants); SAT-029 asks which condition must hold.

I14.why: Distance = constant speed x a time given in mixed units (72 km/h for 25 min, versus 45 mph for 2 h 20 min). Same convert-then-multiply step.
Distance over a time in hours and minutes (1 h 12 min), but the rate is a pace in minutes per mile.

I15.why: Arc length s = r*theta with a radian angle; ACT-660 finds s from r, I15 runs it backward to find r.

I16.why: The x-coordinate of the vertex is the midpoint of the zeros; ACT-734 gives zeros -1 and 7, I16 gives them in factored form (x-2)(x+6).
Minimum of a factored-form quadratic (x-2)(x-8); ACT-330 asks for the minimum value, I16 asks for the x where it occurs.
